answer.rationale: p99 is 5x and confined to primary region. memory_b2 documents that regional failover restored latency fast during a prior degradation and recovered error rates within minutes — that is exactly the mechanism I need. Failing writes risk catastrophic loss, so I will treat failover as the single intervention. I will not rollback the release (memory_b1 shows rollback fixed a checkout spike but releases were stable historically; rollback does not address primary-region-only degradation). I will not enable circuit breaker (memory_b4 — contained a partner dependency, not a same-region internal degradation). I will not route reads (memory_b5 — this is a write-path problem). I will not add capacity until I know whether writes are dropping or just slow — failover first. Memory b2 is the only memory I need to confirm before committing because it is the closest analogue to today and any delta in mechanism (DNS vs L7 shift, drain duration) directly affects whether writes survive the shift during peak settlement. One intervention window means I must get the failover mechanics right on the first attempt.
